memorial_1676-10-06.summary: The Swedish envoys thank Louis XIV for declaring war on Denmark under the guarantee of the Northern treaties and report Charles XI's victory at Halmstad, then press him: turn his arms on Denmark and send troops and ships under the treaty; as Pomponne says that cannot be done, ready a squadron to reach Gothenburg early in spring 1677 and join the ten ships there; the allies will make no peace until France returns its conquests and count on taking Pomerania; any French peace must restore Sweden's lost places; pay an extraordinary subsidy for stores from England and Holland for Stralsund and Gothenburg and for Pomerania; win Hamburg with free trade. Context: the Scanian War (1675-79), with Sweden's German provinces under attack, while the Nijmegen peace talks went on.
memorial_1676-10-06.en:
Same holes as the reading at word level: [?word] = a code given a sense from context, not read; [314: Denmark] = code 314, valued from the 1675 gloss, counted not read; (?) = doubtful. Letters supplied inside words are not marked in the English (see the reading). Which passages are cipher is marked in the reading only. "Your Majesty" is Louis XIV; "the King our master" and "His Majesty" are Charles XI.

Sire, In the state in which the affairs of Sweden stand, His Majesty the King our master could receive no more welcome news than that of the declaration of war which Your Majesty has had published against the King of Denmark under the guarantee of the treaties of the North, since it is a most certain proof of Your Majesty's good intentions and of the exactness with which you carry out the treaties you have with your allies.

despatch_1677-11-24.summary: Bonde reports that the French court is much displeased: someone coming to Livonia, learning of Pac's opposition, means to delay and hold back the [418] (march?) until the matter with Pac is settled, in the form of a vain negotiation, which has alarmed the court. The French want nothing more than the plans, with a prompt diversion into [435] (Prussia?), carried out, and the King's Field Marshal to bring the [418] to ripeness as soon as possible so that the suspicions are dropped. Context (our inference): French-backed plans of late 1677 for a Swedish diversion from Livonia, with the passage of Lithuanian troops, which the despatch of 3/13 Nov 1677 also concerns.
despatch_1677-11-24.en:
Same holes as the reading: [...] = clear lines not transcribed; [418], [435] = numbers with no value; [?word] = a sense from context, not read. Text between asterisks is from cipher. "Your Royal Majesty" is Charles XI; "this court" is the French court.

[...] very ill pleased here at court [...] coming to Livonia and learning of Pac's opposition, would delay and hold back the [418] [?march] until the matter had been settled with Pac, and so [...] in the form of a vain negotiation. I can [say] no more about this [...] the causes that have put this court in such alarm.

To remove that, I have [...] wants nothing more than that the designs, with a prompt diversion into [435] [?Prussia], be carried out to the best advantage, and that Your Royal Majesty's Field Marshal in this regard will bring the [418] [?march] to ripeness as soon as it can ever be done, so that he [...]

despatch_1676-02-12.summary: Bonde reports an overture for an advance of 52,000 riksdaler on the next French subsidy term to buy powder, the banker Adlercrona's refusal to advance money after the Chamber College changed how subsidies were to be paid, the sums assigned to Pomerania, and a request that the French court advance money for a hundred lasts of rye to be shipped to Stade. Context: Sweden's finances early in the Scanian War.

despatch_1676-08-12.summary: The envoys press Pomponne for an increase in the subsidy and for French help by sea and land; he gives no hope of money, yet they learn in confidence that orders are to go to Feuquières to promise an extraordinary subsidy; they then sound him on peace terms and on France giving up its conquests to redeem Sweden's lost places, which he will not commit to before hearing the Allies. NOT FIRST: Wimarson (1903) paraphrases its substance.
despatch_1676-08-12.en:
Made by Claude (Anthropic) from ../readings/1676-08-12.md, page by page, keeping its holes: [...] = a unit not read (code with
no value, cut numeral, weak value or no reading); [?word] = a sense from context or the reader's emendation, not read. Text between
asterisks is from cipher; the rest is clear text as transcribed (approximate). Word codes read from a 1678 gloss (tier H, e.g. 'ekm:t'
= Your Royal Majesty) are translated. Not checked by a person. Not first: Wimarson (1903) II p.176 n.3 and p.305 n.1 give the
substance of this despatch; only the Feuquières passage on 279R is not in his paraphrase.

despatch_1676-10-06.summary: Fragments on French court opinion after the victory at Halmstad, the envoys' memorial and remonstrances to Pomponne, a diversion, French succour, ships and men, and Pomerania. The decode has holes in most sentences.

despatch_1676-10-13.summary: The envoys report that all their requests to the French court have been refused, Lillieroot's leave, France's line that Sweden's state is too desperate for moderate help, fears that Sweden may be forced to a separate peace with Denmark, the House of Lüneburg and Hanover, the withdrawal of subsidies after Halmstad, passports for Swedish ships, and the next campaign (Condé, d'Enghien, Luxembourg).

despatch_1677-11-03.summary: Letters from Béthune: the Lithuanian field commander Pac opposes the diversion Charles XI plans and would refuse his troops passage through Lithuania; France's displeasure; Pufendorf; France's conquests (Luxembourg, Champagne, Charlemont, Mons) and talk of France ceding part of them so that Sweden recovers its own.

despatch_1677-11-17.summary: A numbered report: Pac and the passage of Swedish troops through Samogitia or Courland, Béthune, Adlercrona, Hanover and Saxony, the Margrave of Baden, Queen Christina's furniture in Rome and Cardinal Azzolini, the Elector of Saxony.

despatch_1677-11-24_fr.summary: French counterpart of the Swedish despatch of 24 Nov/4 Dec 1677: a diversion into ducal Prussia with Polish consent, the Marshal's orders to march, and Pac's refusal of passage through Samogitia.

despatch_1677-12-01.summary: Pac's opposition to the passage of Charles XI's troops and the French suspicion that Sweden uses it as a pretext to drop the diversion; Pomponne repeats Béthune's orders to win Pac or advise the Field Marshal to march through Samogitia de facto.

despatch_1677-12-29.summary: Montagu and the Anglo-French peace proposal: Franche-Comté, the barrier towns of Flanders and Hainault, Charleroi and Ath; English preparations (Guernsey, Jersey); the French plan to open the campaign with sieges of Mons, Charlemont, Ypres and Diksmuide; Holstein-Gottorp at Nijmegen.

despatch_1678-01-05.summary: Montagu's armistice proposal (four months against a year and a day), England's promise of satisfaction for Sweden on the barrier, Douai, Lille and Tournai, Ath and Charleroi to be razed, Cardinal d'Estrées, and the Elector of Saxony's secretary.

system: Homophonic substitution on numbers 19-178, one number a letter (a few for ss, st, ff), up to seven homophones a letter (e, f, n), with word codes from about 240 (314 = Danmarck; 335 E.K.M:t, 397 Konung, 418, 435 in the Swedish despatch) and probable nulls…
